世宗懷節皇后父阿古只

units.zh: ◎外戚表 漢外戚有新室之患，晉宗室有八王之難。
units.en: ◎Families of Imperial Consorts Table. Han history warns of the danger consort families posed when Wang Mang seized power; Jin history records the catastrophe of the Rebellion of the Eight Princes.
units.literal: ◎Table of Imperial Consorts' Kin. Under the Han, consort kin had the affliction of the New House; under the Jin, the imperial clan had the calamity of the Eight Princes.

units.zh: 遼史耶律、蕭氏十居八九，宗室、外戚，勢分力敵，相為唇齒，以翰邦家。
units.en: In the Liao annals the Yelü and Xiao families account for nearly all high officeholders; the imperial lineage and the empresses' kin were evenly matched in strength and acted as mutual safeguards of the dynasty.
units.literal: In the Liao histories, the Yelü and Xiao clans make up eight or nine tenths; the imperial clan and consort kin, their power evenly divided, served as each other's lips and teeth to defend the state and house.

units.en: This may have been one workable approach to statecraft.

units.zh: 然以是而興，亦以是而亡，又其法之弊也。
units.en: Yet what raised them also destroyed them—a defect inherent in the system.
units.literal: Yet by this they rose, and by this they perished as well—again a flaw in their law.

units.zh: 契丹外戚，其先曰二審密氏、曰拔里、曰乙室已。
units.en: The Khitan empresses' kin traced their origins to the Two Shimi clans, the Bali, and the Yishi.
units.literal: The Khitan consort kin, their forebears were called the Two Shimi clans, Bali, and Yishi.

units.en: Taizu of Liao took a wife from the Shulü clan.
units.literal: Reaching Liao Taizu, he married a woman of the Shulü clan.

units.en: The Shulü were originally descended from the Uyghur chieftain Nusi.
units.literal: Shulü, originally a descendant of the Uyghur Nusi.

units.zh: 大同元年，太宗自汴將還，留外戚小漢為汴州節度使，賜姓名曰蕭翰，以從中國之俗，由是拔裏、乙室已、述律三族皆為蕭姓。
units.en: In the first year of Datong (947), as Emperor Taizong prepared to withdraw from Kaifeng, he left the consort kinsman Xiaohan as military governor of Bianzhou and bestowed on him the Chinese-style name Xiao Han; thereafter the Bali, Yishi, and Shulü lineages all adopted the surname Xiao in keeping with Chinese custom.
units.literal: In the first year of Datong, when Taizong was about to return from Bian, he left the consort kin Xiao Han as Military Governor of Bianzhou and bestowed the surname and given name Xiao Han, to follow Chinese custom; from this the three clans Bali, Yishi, and Shulü all took the surname Xiao.

units.en: The Bali were divided into two houses, the Great Father and Little Father lines;
units.literal: The Bali had two branches, called Great Father and Little Father;

units.zh: 乙室已亦二房，曰大翁、小翁；
units.en: the Yishi likewise into the Great Elder and Little Elder lines;
units.literal: Yishi likewise had two branches, called Great Elder and Little Elder;

units.zh: 世宗以舅氏塔列葛為國舅別部。
units.en: Emperor Shizong established his uncle Taliege as head of a separate Imperial Uncle division.
units.literal: Emperor Shizong made his maternal uncle Taliege head of the Separate Division of Imperial Uncles.

units.zh: 三族世預北宰相之選，自太祖神冊二年命阿骨只始也。
units.en: All three clans held hereditary claim to the office of Northern Chancellor from Shence 2 (917), when Taizu first appointed Agu Zhi.
units.literal: The three clans from generation to generation were favored in the selection for Northern Chancellor, beginning when Taizu in Shence year 2 appointed Agu Zhi.

units.zh: 聖宗合拔裏、乙室已二國舅帳為一，與別部為二。
units.en: Emperor Shengzong consolidated the Bali and Yishi imperial-uncle households into a single registry, leaving two divisions when the Separate Division is counted.
units.literal: Emperor Shengzong merged the two Imperial Uncle registries of Bali and Yishi into one, making two together with the Separate Division.

units.en: Such is the full account of how the Liao empresses' kin took shape.
units.literal: This is the beginning and end of Liao consort kin.

units.en: Hence the compilation of the Families of Imperial Consorts Table.
units.literal: The 《Table of Imperial Consorts' Kin》 was composed.

units.en: Siwen, father of Empress Ruizhi, consort of Emperor Jingzong
units.literal: Father of Emperor Jingzong's Empress Ruizhi, Siwen

units.zh: 北府宰相繼先。思溫無嗣，睿智皇后命為後。
units.en: Jixian, Northern Chancellor. As Siwen had no male heirs, Empress Ruizhi appointed him as his successor.
units.literal: Northern Chancellor Jixian. Siwen had no heirs; Empress Ruizhi ordered him to be successor.
